original:
Suppose that $A\in{\mathcal{M}}_{n}({\mathbb{Z}})$ , with $A\neq kI_{n}$ for any constant $k$ . We have

 $\#\operatorname{C}(A,{\mathbb{Z}};H)\ll H^{n^{2}-2n+2}.$ 

Furthermore for $n\geq 4$ , if $A$ is not similar to neither $\alpha I_{1}\oplus\beta I_{n-1}$ nor $\alpha I_{n}+\beta E_{1,2}$ , we have

 $\#\operatorname{C}(A,{\mathbb{Z}};H)\ll H^{n^{2}-4n+8}.$ 

In addition, we also have

 $\#\operatorname{C}(A,{\mathbb{Z}};H)\gg H^{n},$ 

which is sharp when, for example, $A$ has $n$ distinct eigenvalues. All implied constants depend on $A$ .
